title: Changing from Joe Robichaux's style to a modern style
summary: He once played like Joe Robichaux but shortened his left hand and used four-part harmony for small combos.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You say you changed your style, uh, how did you, how did you change?

Well, you ever heard Joe Robichaud play? Yes. I used to play like Joe Robichaud. That was, that's the man who taught. But I changed more, more modern because the fellas were telling me that the way I was playing, it was hard, with a small combo, see? For me to play like that. So when it was my solo, I had to play my solo. So what I would do, I always had the bass player helping, see? So they told me I could shorten up my left hand to plenty. And, uh, use more four-part harmony.
Yeah, that's the bass player. Like Joe does, a lot of chords up there, right in the treble. That's right.
